stories.headline: 'Terrorist can return only in handcuffs': Bangladesh on Hasina's homecoming request
stories.bodyText:
Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir on Tuesday ruled out an unconditional return for deposed former prime minister 
Sheikh Hasina
, saying she could be brought back from India only "in handcuffs or under strict surveillance". The remarks came after reports that Hasina had sought to return to Bangladesh on December 16, the country's Victory Day.
"She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance," Kobir told reporters after briefing foreign diplomats on the situation in Bangladesh at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka, according to the state-run Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS).
He was responding to a Reuters report that Hasina, who has been living in India since leaving Bangladesh in August 2024, wanted to return on Victory Day, which marks the country's independence from Pakistan in 1971.
"A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," Kobir said, according to BSS.
According to The Daily Star, the minister also said, "The reality is that no terrorist will ever be allowed to return this way without extradition."
"The people of Bangladesh see terrorism as coming from one source -- Awami terrorism, sponsored by Hasina from Delhi. Everyone knows this. It's not rocket science," he added.
Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali had told Reuters that the former prime minister wanted the Bangladesh government to arrange her return from Delhi aboard the national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
"Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali told Reuters.
"Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th," he added.
Kobir also addressed concerns over sporadic attacks in Bangladesh, alleging that Awami League supporters were behind incidents intended to frighten the public and accusing Hasina of sponsoring them. "(But) the attacks had failed to intimidate people," he said, according to The Daily Star.
Asked how the government planned to handle the situation, Kobir said it was confident in its ability to respond. "We stand firmly with the people at all times. We're dealing with the situation confidently and taking our people into confidence," he said, as quoted by the newspaper.
The briefing was attended by heads of diplomatic missions, United Nations agencies and international organisations, according to a note circulated by the foreign ministry.

stories.headline: President Murmu to inaugurate Bali Jatra in Cuttack during two-day Odisha visit
stories.deck: She will stay overnight at Lok Bhavan and attend the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy in Bhubaneswar on November 25
stories.bodyText:
President Droupadi Murmu will arrive in Odisha on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon on a two-day visit, during which she will inaugurate the Bali Jatra festival in Cuttack and attend a national convention on homoeopathy in Bhubaneswar, officials said.
After arriving at the Biju Patnaik International Airport in Bhubaneswar, Ms. Murmu will proceed to Lok Bhavan before travelling to Cuttack to inaugurate the annual trade fair this evening, they said.
She will stay overnight at Lok Bhavan and attend the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday (November 25).
Security has been tightened in the twin cities of Bhubaneswar and Cuttack ahead of the President's visit.
DGP Vinaytosh Mishra reviewed security arrangements at the Bali Jatra ground in Cuttack on Monday (November 23).
Around 70 platoons of police personnel will be deployed to manage security and crowd movement, he said.
Police have also set up 38 watchtowers and installed 1,400 CCTV cameras at the venue, another official said.
In Bhubaneswar, arrangements have been made to ensure smooth traffic movement. Traffic restrictions will be imposed for brief periods to facilitate the movement of the President's convoy, he said.

stories.headline: Musk's SpaceX and Tesla entrusts five directors for merger talks: Reports
stories.bodyText:
The boards of 
Elon Musk
's 
SpaceX
 and Tesla have appointed five directors to special committees tasked with overseeing discussions on a potential merger between the two companies, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday citing people familiar with the matter.
The appointments include two directors from SpaceX, Roelof Botha and Randy Glein and three from Tesla, Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung.
Musk said during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that merging his AI, robotics, electric vehicle (EV) and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate umbrella would be "a good idea".
He also confirmed that the two companies had formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential merger.
The committees have hired financial advisers to prepare models that will help determine their negotiating positions in a potential all-stock merger, the FT reported.
SpaceX has hired Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, while Tesla has appointed Evercore as its adviser, according to the report.
The bankers are also assessing areas of overlap between the businesses and how a combined company could be structured.
A potential merger would face significant regulatory challenges, particularly because of SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's dependence on China, the report said.
Bloomberg reported earlier this month that a deal could be announced as early as December, citing progress in merger negotiations.

stories.headline: Audi India to hike vehicle prices by up to 2% from January 1
stories.bodyText:
Audi India to hike vehicle prices by up to 2% from January 1
The latest hike marks Audi India's second price revision in 2026, as the automaker had previously raised prices by up to 2 per cent across its model range from April 1 this year.
Audi India to hike vehicle prices by up to 2% from January 1.
Credit: Reuters
New Delhi: German luxury carmaker Audi on Tuesday said it will increase ex-showroom prices of its models in India by up to 2 per cent with effect from January 1, 2027, to offset rising input costs.
The latest hike marks Audi India's second price revision in 2026, as the automaker had previously raised prices by up to 2 per cent across its model range from April 1 this year.
The price revision will be applicable across its model range, the company said in a statement.
"In response to rising input costs, we will be implementing a price revision of up to 2 per cent. This adjustment is essential to maintaining the long-term sustainability of our business. We have kept this revision as measured as possible, and our focus remains on giving customers an ownership experience that solidifies their trust in the brand," Audi India Brand Director Balbir Singh Dhillon said.
Audi India's current portfolio comprises a range of luxury sedans and SUVs, including the A4 and A6 sedans and the Q3, Q5, Q7 and Q8 SUVs. Its performance-oriented offerings include the SQ8 and RS Q8. The company also sells the Q3 in India, with the latest generation launched in October 2026 and locally assembled at the Volkswagen Group's facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra.

briefs.headline: Punjab Assembly polls: BJP-SAD to hold joint presser today
briefs.deck: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal will address the meeting at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi at 1 p.m.
briefs.bodyText:
As the political climate heats up ahead of next year’s Assembly polls in Punjab, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are set to hold a joint press conference in New Delhi today (November 24, 2026).
Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal will address the meeting at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi at 1 p.m.
While no further information is available on the subject of the presser, it is widely anticipated that the two parties will provide details on the alliance for the Punjab Assembly polls. Negotiations on seat-sharing between the BJP and the SAD for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls have been underway.
The SAD had snapped its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the now-scrapped three farm laws.
Earlier, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal was also part of the Modi government as a Minister with Cabinet rank.
Last month in Delhi, Shah had predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027. When he came to Chandigarh on November 1, he again said an NDA government will be formed in the border State.
The statement reignited the buzz about a possible SAD-BJP alliance.
On November 2, when SAD president Badal was asked about the possibility of a re-alliance, he gave a guarded response to speculation, saying, "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen".
He reiterated that, except for the Congress and the AAP, he is open to an alliance with other parties which accept his party's philosophy.
In the 2022 Assembly polls, the BJP won two seats, and the SAD could register victories in three Assembly segments out of a total of 117.
Prior to the end of the electoral alliance, both the Akalis and the BJP used to contest together. As per the previous pact in the Assembly polls, the BJP used to contest 23 seats and the SAD 94 Assembly seats.
In parliamentary polls, the SAD used to fight for 10 seats and the BJP the remaining three.
(With inputs from PTI)

briefs.headline: T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told
briefs.deck: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to take instructions from the woman officer, too, and report to the court by November 24, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh of misbehaving with her, as widely reported in the media over the past few days.
Also read: Collector files complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA
Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer.
When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case.
“Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?”
The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.”
On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.”
‘Won’t interfere if there’s no plaint’
Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.”
After taking note of the SPP’s submission that the State was willing to file an affidavit before the court making it clear that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received any complaint from the woman IAS officer, the judge asked Mr. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any complaint.

briefs.headline: Cargo driver killed after being knocked down by truck near Kasimedu harbour
briefs.bodyText:
A 61-year-old man died after being knocked down by an unidentified container truck near the Kasimedu fishing harbour on Monday (November 23, 2026) night.
A senior official from the City Traffic Police said the deceased, Lakshmanan, was a resident of Kanni Koil Street in Tiruvottiyur and worked as a driver of a cargo rickshaw used to transport ice and fish at the Kasimedu fishing harbour.
On Monday night, after completing his duty, Lakshmanan was attempting to cross the service road at the Kasimedu fishing harbour. At that moment, an unidentified container truck, which was travelling at high speed, hit him and fled the scene without stopping. As it was raining heavily and there was little traffic on the harbour road, no one came forward to rescue him or take him to hospital. Having suffered severe head and body injuries, he died, the police official added.
The Washermanpet Traffic Investigation Wing police, who were informed of the accident belatedly, sent Lakshmanan’s body to Government Stanley Hospital for a post-mortem examination.
The police are examining CCTV footage from cameras installed in the area to identify the container truck involved in the accident.

briefs.headline: A red bra, Nvidia flag and 'bloodied' CEO: Trump shares AI photo of Jensen Huang after Nvidia comeback
briefs.bodyText:
In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump shared an edited version of his famous photo taken moments after he survived an assassination attempt in Pennsylvania in July 2024. 
The photo shared by Trump shows Huang and an NVIDIA flag in the background instead of an American flag.  The highlight of the photo, however, is Huang, with blood splattered on his face, triumphantly holding a red bra over his head.
"Congratulations to NVIDIA on having made, what I consider to be, an absolutely GREAT decision!" Trump wrote before posting the photo.
"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk.
Eleven days after he announed his resignation and six days after his offer to return as CEO was rejected, the company on Monday said Huang had returned as CEO, effective immediately.
On Monday Trump said he played a key role in bringing back Huang, throwing his weight behind the scandal-hit CEO. "He did nothing wrong," Trump said, calling Huang "a genius".
“The United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security,” Trump said in a social media post Monday, soon after Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s return. “The attorney general of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
Later, speaking to The New York Times, Trump, while declining to answer questions about whether he believes that Alice Huang was working with Chinese intelligence agencies, said that he had checked with senior officials as to whether Jensen Huang had any direct role in chip smuggling and was assured that he did not.
“All those guys knew about it,” Trump said.
“I wouldn’t have handled it the way he handled it,” Trump told the publication. “The Peyton Place part,” the President said, a reference to the 1960s-era soap opera based on a novel about a town roiled in constant sex scandals.
“Without that, it would have been a lot easier because that got the attention,” he added. “You know, sex was involved, and sex sells better than stocks.”
Huang was forced to resign as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

briefs.headline: Mumbai Police take action against 12 at Mahalaxmi concert using new anti-narcotics forensic van
briefs.deck: The deployment at the Mahalaxmi concert marked one of the van’s first operational uses, coming just a day after its inauguration
briefs.bodyText:
The Mumbai Police’s Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) took action against 12 persons allegedly found to have consumed narcotic substances during a live music event at Mahalaxmi Racecourse on Sunday (November 22, 2026), a day after deploying a newly introduced mobile investigation and forensic van equipped to conduct preliminary drug testing at event venues.
According to a press note issued by the Mumbai Police on Monday (November 23, 2026), the specially equipped Anti-Narcotics Investigation and Forensic Van was deployed at the ‘AEDEN’ live music event at Mahalaxmi Racecourse, where police screened attendees using advanced equipment.
During the screening, 12 persons were allegedly found to have consumed narcotic substances, following which action was initiated against them under the relevant anti-narcotics laws, the police said.
The van, which was inaugurated by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on November 21, 2026, has been developed to strengthen the ANC’s efforts to prevent drug consumption, trafficking and distribution across Mumbai.
According to the police, the vehicle is equipped with facilities to conduct preliminary examinations of suspected narcotic substances at crime scenes, collect samples, photograph and record video evidence, and manage seized materials. These procedures can be carried out at a single location, reducing the need for separate arrangements during investigations.
The police said the mobile forensic facility would enable officers to conduct immediate checks at crowded venues, public gatherings and locations suspected of drug consumption or distribution.
The deployment at the Mahalaxmi concert marked one of the van’s first operational uses, coming just a day after its inauguration.
The operation was carried out by the ANC’s Worli unit under the supervision of senior Crime Branch officials, including Deputy Commissioner of Police Pournima Chougule-Shringi and Assistant Commissioner of Police Sudhir Hirdekar.
The Mumbai Police said the introduction of the specialised vehicle was part of its broader efforts to strengthen preventive measures and enforcement against narcotic substances through the use of modern technology.

briefs.headline: Dog menace on rise in Hamirpur, close to 6,000 people bitten in 2026
briefs.deck: The Health Department data shines a light on the canine crisis, which is not limited to stray dogs
briefs.bodyText:
A total of 5,876 people were bitten by dogs in Himachal Pradesh’s Hamirpur district over 10 months this year, averaging 19 bite cases daily.
The Health Department data shines a light on the canine crisis, which is not limited to stray dogs.
Between January and October this year, stray dogs accounted for 3,863 bite cases, while pet dogs were involved in 2,013.
The number of reported cases this year has already exceeded the total for the entire previous year by 1,551. On average, nearly 19 people have been targeted by dogs every day.
"Dog bite cases must be taken seriously. People should not be negligent if bitten or scratched by a dog and should immediately visit the nearest healthcare facility for treatment. It is essential to complete the full course of the anti-rabies vaccine as per medical advice," Hamirpur chief medical officer Dr Satish Kumar said on Monday (November 23, 2026).
Allowing pet dogs to roam freely in public spaces, failing to maintain proper control and negligence in their care are posing a risk to public safety too, he said.
In Hamirpur town, the worst-hit areas are the Hirangar forest region and Anu zone, as stray dogs are found in great numbers on the Hamirpur-Sujanpur main road and near the Ano chowk. Students exercising here are targeted by the dogs, with residents alleging that the local municipal corporation is silent on this issue.
The number of people bitten by stray dogs in 2026 was 445 in January, 420 in February, 382 in March, 396 in April, 425 in May, 444 in June, 294 in July, 428 in August, 321 in September, and 308 in October.
Meanwhile, regarding pet dogs, the number of people injured by them was 164 in January, 212 in February, 234 in March, 188 in April, 224 in May, 208 in June, 192 in July, 191 in August, 220 in September, and 180 in October.
Treating a dog bite as a minor injury can prove costly. Rabies is a serious and life-threatening disease, but it can be prevented through timely treatment and vaccination. If bitten or scratched by a dog, immediately wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, health officials said.
“Regardless of whether the wound is small or large, consult a doctor without delay. Complete the full course of the rabies vaccine as advised by the physician. Do not apply turmeric, chilli, soil, oil, or any other substances to the wound,” they added.

briefs.headline: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
briefs.deck: Nvidia’s board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, pressured by U.S. authorities, sparked a rapid stock rally but left the company facing multiple investigations, including an SEC probe and a shareholder lawsuit over governance
briefs.bodyText:
Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO at the urging of U.S. President Donald Trump, less than two weeks after the co-founder of the AI chip powerhouse resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.
Also Read: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
The reported ties between Mr. Huang and a suspected spy led to his resignation as CEO. They sparked investigations by the U.S. securities regulator and the FBI, congressional hearings, a review by the company’s independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit.
Below is a ‌look at how the rehiring, which sparked a massive rally in Nvidia’s stock, could impact the legal exposure for the company and its directors.
What are the allegations?
Mr. Huang allegedly had intimate relations with Alice Huang, an unrelated Chinese businesswoman who is accused of having ties to Beijing. Mr. Huang is also accused of having had intimate relationships with at least two Nvidia employees. He resigned on November 12.
Also Read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal
Mr. Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised, but has not publicly addressed the alleged relationships in detail. China has denied the espionage allegations. Attempts by Reuters to reach Ms. Alice Huang have been unsuccessful.
Nvidia said in a statement that, based on U.S. government input, the board ‌was confident that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” a claim backed by Mr. Trump in an interview with CNBC. Mr. Trump said that Mr. Huang did nothing wrong and that his intervention led to Mr. Huang’s return.
Nvidia sits at the centre of the technological rivalry between the United States and China. Washington has ‌imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since 2022, including those made by Nvidia.
Could the board be on the hook despite Trump’s Assurances?
An investor ‌filed a so-called derivative lawsuit in federal court on November 11, seeking to hold the board liable for failing to make a good-faith effort to oversee the business and Mr. Huang. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia to make repeated assurances about Mr. Huang’s relationship with Ms. Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, until the allegations were public.
Also Read: Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns
Nvidia formed a committee of independent directors that hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to assist in an internal investigation. The committee is still investigating, Nvidia said on Monday (November 23, 2026).
Mr. Trump’s statement that Mr. Huang did not pose a national security risk could strengthen the directors’ legal defences, according to legal experts. The directors could argue ‌that Mr. Trump’s assurances mean the company will not be prosecuted for export control violations, removing the threat that rehiring Mr. Huang could damage the company.
However, Lee Squitieri, one of the attorneys representing the shareholder in the derivative lawsuit, told Reuters in an email that rehiring Mr. Huang does not change the liability scenario very much and that the problems extend beyond possible export control violations. Mr. Squitieri said Mr. Huang dominated the board and harmed Nvidia by leaving it without a succession plan and with poor compliance oversight and ‌weak corporate governance.
Derivative lawsuit settlements are generally paid from insurance, and Nvidia has coverage for its officers and directors of up to $950 million.
What happens to any federal criminal probe?
Mr. Trump has said the FBI is investigating Mr. Huang’s affair with Ms. Alice Huang, but has been vague about the focus of the probe.
Also Read: Nvidia to reveal first earnings since spy scandal
Attorney General Todd Blanche said on November 12 the FBI is investigating Ms. Alice Huang. The Department of Justice has said it had no evidence of wrongdoing by Nvidia or its co-founder.
Reuters could not immediately determine the status of federal criminal probes, and the Justice Department declined to comment.
Legal experts said Mr. Trump’s remarks on Monday (November 23) make it unlikely the Justice Department would continue an investigation during his administration, particularly given how much influence the president wields over the department.
But the statute of limitations for export ‌control violations extends beyond January 2029, when Mr. Trump leaves office, and a new attorney general could reopen an investigation. Mr. Trump also could preemptively pardon Mr. Huang to avoid future prosecution for violating federal law.
Can states still pursue cases againts Mr. Huang and the company?
Attorneys general in Missouri and California said on Monday (November 23) their investigations will continue.
The office of California Attorney General Rob Bonta, a Democrat, said on November 19 that it had served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia to determine if China obtained advanced chips or confidential information and whether Nvidia misled the public. Bonta has not said whether the investigation is criminal or civil in nature, and a probe does not mean a case will be brought.
The office of Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, a Republican, said it would proceed with its investigation into whether Mr. Huang’s actions harmed state pension funds. Her office previously said it was viewing the investigation through a consumer ‌protection lens focused on potential misrepresentations.
What happens to the SEC probe?
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia for potential accounting issues, Reuters reported on Friday (November 20). Reuters could not immediately ascertain on Monday (November 23) whether Mr. Trump’s intervention had changed the status of that federal probe.
The SEC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
However, the independence of the SEC, which is structured as a bipartisan commission and is chaired by Mr. Trump appointee Paul Atkins, has eroded under Mr. Trump’s second administration, according to legal experts.
In March, Reuters reported that the SEC’s enforcement chief quit after just six months on the job after clashing with the agency’s leaders over the direction of its enforcement program, including the handling of cases with ties to Mr. Trump and his family.
Do investors have legal recourse?
A proposed class action was filed in San Jose, California, federal court on November 9, alleging the company and Mr. Huang defrauded shareholders by concealing the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which Mr. Jensen Huang described in an October 30 ‌Bloomberg interview as “normal and not unusual.”
The lawsuit did not specify damages but the stock lost around 20% from its peak to the end of the class period, a decline of around $1 trillion in market value.
The stock rally sparked by rehiring Mr. Huang could undermine the value of the lawsuit if the shares continue to rise. U.S. securities law caps shareholder damages if the stock rebounds in 90 days after an initial drop.
Published - November 24, 2026 12:22 pm IST

stories.headline: Bengaluru man gets Rs 4 ‘location surcharge’ on medicines, fights MedPlus in consumer court, pharmacy ordered to pay Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 2,000 costs
stories.deck: A 36-year-old resident of Sarjapura challenged a Rs 4 surcharge levied by the pharmacy chain MedPlus. The district consumer court ruled against MedPlus for engaging in unfair trade practices, deeming the surcharge unlawful since medicines were sold at their maximum retail price. Consequently, MedPlus was ordered to refund the surcharge and provide compensation for mental distress and legal…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: It was only Rs 4, but a 36-year-old Sarjapura resident refused to let it go. Charged a "location surcharge" on top of the printed price of his medicines, he fought it for months, first by email and then in the consumer court. The Bangalore (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now held pharmacy chain MedPlus guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.
The dispute began on September 25, 2025, when the complainant bought medicines from the MedPlus Pharmacy outlet in Sarjapura for Rs 1,113. The invoice carried an extra line, "Location Surcharge Fees", of Rs 4, inclusive of GST, even though medicines are sold at the maximum retail price (MRP).
He emailed the company the same day and sent follow-ups and reminders until October 3, asking for a refund and for the practice to stop. The company's reply, the commission noted, was that "ongoing maintenance costs" across its locations had forced it to introduce a small surcharge to help maintain its shops. He received no refund, only a reply citing maintenance costs.
On January 19, 2026, he approached the commission, appearing in person. 
He sought a refund of Rs 4, Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 10,000 for litigation and incidental costs. Optival Health Solutions Pvt. Ltd., which operates MedPlus, and its Sarjapura branch did not appear despite notice, nor did they file a reply. The commission placed them ex parte.
Relying on a National Commission ruling, Kotak Mahindra Old Mutual vs Dr Nishi Gupta, the commission held that not filing a written version amounts to admission of the complaint's allegations. It added that the company's own email replies admitted the surcharge was being collected, and that the invoice showed it plainly.
The commission rejected the maintenance argument. It said the MRP already covers taxes, retailer margin, transport and maintenance, and that shop upkeep is a business overhead to be met from the retailer's profit margin. It cannot be passed on to customers as a fee without prior disclosure and consent. It noted that charging above MRP is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and that the Legal Metrology rules and the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, bar the sale of medicines above the printed MRP. Consumer fora, it said, have consistently held that no retailer can charge even a rupee over MRP under labels such as handling or convenience fees.
The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, on October 30 allowed the complaint in part. stories.headline: Bengaluru man deposits Rs 2.5L in FD with cooperative society, but society stops paying after June 2024, consumer commission orders it to return Rs 2.5L with 13% interest and Rs 25k as compensation
stories.deck: A Bengaluru commission ordered Aishwarya Co-operative Society to repay a fixed deposit of Rs 2.5 lakh. The society failed to pay interest after June 2024, constituting a clear deficiency in service. The complainant, Gangadharaiah, sought higher interest rates and compensation for mental agony. He had made multiple requests for payment and renewal without a satisfactory response.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The Bengaluru Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Aishwarya Co-operative Society Ltd to repay a 65-year-old man's Rs 2.5 lakh fixed deposit with interest at 13% per annum, holding that its failure to pay interest after June 2024 amounted to deficiency in service.
In an order dated September 30, 2026, the commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, partly allowed the complaint filed by Gangadharaiah of Narasimhaiahnapalya, Magadi Main Road, against the society's president. The society, based in Rajajinagar, did not appear and was placed ex parte.
The direction
The society must pay the matured FD amount of Rs 2,50,000 along with 13% annual interest from June 2024 till realisation. It must also pay Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. All dues must be cleared within 45 days of the order.
The commission allowed the complaint only in part. Gangadharaiah had sought 18% interest from the date of complaint and Rs 2 lakh in damages for mental agony.
The case
Gangadharaiah said he deposited Rs 2.5 lakh with the society on July 6, 2021 at 13% interest, with the society agreeing to pay interest monthly, which came to Rs 2,700. 
An FD receipt (No. 062) was issued for July 6, 2021 to July 6, 2022, and the deposit was renewed (No. 988) for July 6, 2022 to July 6, 2023.
The society paid interest till June 2024, he said, after which it stopped paying and did not renew the FD. His requests for renewal and the dues drew no satisfactory reply, he alleged.
He wrote to the Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies and other authorities on November 12, 2024 and February 13, 2025, seeking payment of the principal and interest within 15 days, but got no response. A legal notice was served on July 9, 2025, which the society also did not comply with. The complaint was filed on September 24, 2025.
Why the commission ruled for the depositor
The society did not appear despite service of notice, and filed neither a written version nor evidence. The commission relied on the complainant's affidavit and documents, including the FD certificates, letters to the registrar, the legal notice, and postal and tracking receipts.
It noted that the society had accepted the deposit and agreed to pay 13% interest, and had paid it till June 2024. It said the society had not explained why it stopped paying thereafter, and that the default was a clear violation of FD terms by a financial institution.
The complaint was filed under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Gangadharaiah was represented by advocate S B Vishwanath.

stories.headline: Man suffers serious spinal injuries after concrete pole falls on car in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
A 40-year-old man suffered spinal fractures after a concrete pole while being lifted by a crane fell on his moving car on New BEL Road near Mayuri Junction around midnight on November 18.
Shreyas N.K., a businessman, was on his way home when he stopped near the work site and asked the workers about the diversion. The workers directed him to take another route, which he followed. But as he drove past the site, the pole fell on his car, leaving him with serious spine injuries.
The car was damaged in the impact. Shreyas, who was driving alone, was rushed to a nearby private hospital, where doctors said he might need immediate surgery. His family later shifted him to another private hospital in the city, where he was admitted to the ICU. His treatment is continuing.
The family has filed a complaint, following which an FIR was registered at the Sadashivanagar Police Station.
Shreyas’s brother has also written to the Malleshwaram MLA C.N. Ashwath Narayan and Bescom, seeking an inquiry into the incident and accountability from those responsible for the work.
Victim’s brother, Tejas Khoday, also addressed a press conference on Monday. Mr. Khoday said the crane operator and the workers left the spot after the accident without checking on his brother or helping him. The family tried contacting the contractor, but received no response.
He questioned why the road had not been completely blocked if a concrete pole was being lifted, and said accountability should extend beyond the crane operator to those who had authorised and supervised the work. “If work of this nature is being carried out, with the risk of endangering lives, shouldn’t the entire road be closed to traffic? Those responsible must face stringent action,” he said.
Mr. Khoday said the family has received no response from the Bescom or the MLA, and that the inquiry should establish who had commissioned the work, hired the crane and supervised the operation. “We wrote to the MLA and Bescom on November 20. We are still waiting for a response. At the very least, the authorities should acknowledge the complaint and tell us what action is being taken.”
The accident is among several incidents in Bengaluru in which people using public roads have been injured or killed by falling infrastructure or hazards arising from civic and construction work. In March 2025, two women, one of them pregnant, were killed when an electric pole fell on them during road repair work in Suddaguntepalya. In January that year, a 15-year-old girl was killed when a wooden pole fell from an under-construction building in V.V. Puram. In January 2023, an under-construction Metro pillar collapsed on a motorcycle on Hennur Main Road, killing a woman and her two-year-old son

The Karnataka Tourism Department has decided to upgrade select Jungle Lodges and Resorts (JLR) properties and explore new eco-tourism activities, with a focus on promoting nature-based tourism without compromising forest ecosystems and wildlife conservation.

George on Monday directed department officials to identify suitable forest areas, including Muthodi Nature Camp, and examine the feasibility of introducing new safari, trekking and other nature-based tourism activities after obtaining the necessary statutory approvals from the Forest Department.
He said that priority would be given to improving accommodation, cleanliness, hospitality and visitor amenities at key JLR properties, including Kabini, Bandipur and Kemmannugundi. “Repair and renovation works would be undertaken without disturbing the natural character of the properties. Detailed project reports would be prepared wherever necessary,” he said.
The Minister said that the initiative also aimed to create employment opportunities for local communities by involving them as nature guides and service providers in hospitality, food, transport and other allied tourism activities. This would ensure that the income generated through eco-tourism directly benefits local residents.
Tourism Department Secretary Ram Prasath Manohar said “the Forest Department, Karnataka Eco Tourism Development Board (KEDB) and JLR would coordinate to expand eco-tourism through a regulated and sustainable model.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka urges Toyota to treble output to 10L units, bring Japan taxi hybrids
briefs.deck: In a significant move for the automotive sector, Karnataka has pledged its support to Toyota Motor as they look to ramp up vehicle production to 10 lakh units. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar and Industries Minister MB Patil recently held discussions with Toyota leaders about innovative mobility solutions and encouraged investment exploration at the upcoming Global Investors' Meet.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU/MOTOMACHI (JAPAN): 
Karnataka
 has offered full support to Toyota Motor to expand its operations in the state and raise vehicle production capacity to 10 lakh units, even as it pushed the carmaker to bring its affordable hybrid taxi model to make urban transport cheaper.
Chief minister DK Shivakumar and industries minister MB Patil discussed the proposal and new mobility opportunities with Toyota's senior leadership at its Motomachi plant in Japan on Monday. Toyota's Bidadi plant, near Bengaluru, currently has an annual output of over 3.5 lakh vehicles.
The talks focused on Toyota's Japan taxi, a low-cost hybrid electric vehicle built for commercial use. Its introduction could give commuters a cheaper, cleaner cab option. Flex-fuel vehicles were also discussed as part of efforts to promote alternative fuels.
Toyota invited for next yr’s GIM
Toyota’s delegation, led by chairman, managing director and CEO Masakazu Yoshimura, highlighted Karnataka’s importance as a manufacturing and export hub and outlined its existing operations in the state, according to the CM’s office. Shivakumar and Patil invited Toyota to the Global Investors’ Meet to be held early next year to explore more investments, as the state seeks to widen its industrial base and create jobs.
The ministers toured the Motomachi plant, Toyota’s first flagship passenger car facility in Asia, set up in 1959. It assembles hybrid, battery electric and fuel cell vehicles.
They also met over 20 Karnataka ITI graduates undergoing specialised training in Japan under Toyota’s Global Skill-up programme, and urged them to use the exposure to sharpen their skills.
The delegation also visited the Toyota Kaikan Museum. Earlier, the two travelled from Tokyo to Nagoya on the Shinkansen, a bullet train. In a video shared on X, Shivakumar cited Japan’s high-speed rail network as an example of how technology and infrastructure can transform transport.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru bizman injured as pole crashes on moving car, family blames Bescom for shoddy work
briefs.deck: A disturbing incident unfolded on New BEL Road when a cement pole unexpectedly collapsed onto Shreyas Khoday's vehicle, injuring him in the process. Shockingly, neither the crane operator nor any nearby workers offered assistance. His brother, Tejas, voiced serious concerns about the negligence displayed by government officials during construction projects. This alarming event starkly parallels a…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A city-based businessman had a narrow escape when a cement pole, which was lifted by a crane, snapped and fell on his car on New BEL Road in Sadashivanagar.
The injured, Shreyas Khoday, is undergoing treatment.
According to Shreyas’ younger brother, Tejas, a cement pole being lifted by a crane fell on the car in the intervening night of Nov 17 and 18. “My brother was alone in the car and was driving near the Punjab National Bank junction when he noticed some men diverting traffic. One of them told him that Bescom was carrying out work and traffic was being temporarily diverted. My brother slowly drove along the diverted route when a cement pole being lifted by a crane fell on his car, denting its roof. He sustained injuries to his head and other parts of the body. Instead of helping him, the crane operator and other workers fled the spot,” Tejas said.
Tejas lodged a police complaint and also tried to reach Bescom officials but did not get a response.
“Therefore, I decided to bring the incident to the media’s attention. Govt agencies must ensure the utmost caution while carrying out work in public places. This incident shows how carelessly such work is handled. 
Worse, the crane operator and other workers fled without even checking on the occupants of the car. What if there had been more people in the car, including children? What if the occupants had been newcomers to the city, unfamiliar with the area and unsure of what to do?” he asked.
TOI tried to contact the Bescom chief engineer-north, but in vain.
According to Sadashivnagar police, they have contacted the engineer concerned, asking him to share details of the persons responsible for the mishap.
D
isaster in the past
According to Tejas, the incident brought back painful memories of the Jan 10, 2023, tragedy in which 28-year-old software engineer Tejaswini Sulakhe and her two-and-a-half-year-old son, Vihan, died after a massive 40-foot-tall steel reinforcement cage for a Metro pillar collapsed onto a busy road near HBR Layout (Nagawara). Tejaswini’s husband was also injured in the incident.
“Why doesn’t the govt wake up and ensure that such work is carried out with proper care? Why is there so much apathy in handling these projects? Why are govt officials so negligent about the safety of the public?” he asked.

briefs.headline: 11 unauthorised transactions drain Rs 42.4 lakh from Bengaluru firm in 30 minutes
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A series of 11 unauthorised bank transfers drained Rs 42.5 lakh from a private firm’s corporate account in just 30 minutes, leaving the company scrambling to stop further debits. The transactions, carried out through IMPS, bypassed the mandatory OTP-based approval process. Despite immediately alerting the bank and seeking to freeze the account, the company could not prevent the money from being transferred to multiple unknown accounts.
According to a complaint filed by the accountant of the restaurant company (Popo Global Pvt Ltd), the company maintains a current account with a private bank (HDFC) at its Jayanagar branch and uses its corporate net banking platform to process vendor payments and staff salaries.
The company’s payment system involves a two-level approval process. Beneficiaries are first added by the accounts department using its login credentials, after which payment requests are forwarded to the directors for approval through their respective login credentials. OTP-based authentication is mandatory for approving transactions.
However, on Nov 12, around 2.30 pm, the company noticed an unexpected debit from its current account without any authentication. 
It contacted the bank and attempted to freeze further debit transactions. However, within next 30 minutes, 11 unauthorised IMPS transactions were carried out, transferring a total of Rs 42,49,689 to multiple accounts.
The first transaction, amounting to Rs 2 lakh, was recorded at 2.33 pm in the name of Manas Das. Subsequently, five more transactions were made to different beneficiaries. Four transactions were credited to an account in the name of Sunrise Enterprise, with individual transfers ranging from Rs 4,99,890 to Rs 4,99,990. Two other transactions, amounting to Rs 2 lakh and Rs 3 lakh, were made in the names of Anand Rajendran and Ranjana Yadev, respectively. Another two transfers of Rs 4,99,910 and Rs 4,99,989 went to Jai Maa Bhadrakali Enterprises. The remaining transaction of Rs 1.5 lakh was transferred to an account belonging to Devendra Singh.
A case has been registered at East Cyber Crime police station under Information Technology Act and section 318 (cheating) of BNS. A senior officer said the complainant has provided the transaction details, including dates, timestamps, beneficiary names, bank identifiers and account numbers.
The frauds involving corporate bank accounts usually happen through compromised net banking credentials, malware, phishing or manipulation of the bank’s beneficiary and approval process. However, there are several possible ways such a fraud could have been executed.
Tips to stay safe
-Use separate devices for initiating and approving transactions.
-Enable transaction alerts for every debit and beneficiary addition.
-Set daily transaction limits and beneficiary-wise transfer limits.
-Introduce a cooling period before newly added beneficiaries can receive large payments.
-Restrict remote access software and unauthorised applications on computers used for banking.
-Contact the bank immediately and report unauthorised transactions through the cybercrime helpline 1930.

briefs.headline: Dating app video call turns into sextortion trap, Bengaluru man loses Rs 2.2 lakh
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 29-year-old man working with a private firm was allegedly blackmailed by cyber fraudsters after a woman he met on a dating app recorded an intimate video call and threatened to circulate the footage among his family, friends and professional contacts unless he paid money.
According to the complaint filed by Adam (name changed), a resident of Indiranagar, he connected with a woman identifying herself as Kanika on the dating app Aisle on Nov 2. After exchanging a few messages on 
WhatsApp
, she initiated a video call during which she allegedly appeared nude. Adam said he disconnected the call and blocked her.
However, the incident soon escalated into a cyber extortion racket. Unknown persons contacted him, claiming to have screenshots and a recording of the video call, along with access to his 
Instagram
 contacts. They threatened to circulate the intimate footage with them.
A man later contacted Adam and demanded money, instructing him to purchase gift cards from Amazon Pay, Nykaa and Tata CLiQ and share the redemption details. Fearing public humiliation and the circulation of the recording, Adam allegedly complied with the demands. He purchased 19 gift cards worth Rs 1.9 lakh. Soon, he noticed additional unauthorised transactions involving his cards and bank accounts. His total financial loss is estimated at Rs 2,21,154, although the exact amount is subject to verification and reconciliation of transaction records.
Suspecting a coordinated cyber extortion and financial fraud operation involving multiple individuals, Adam approached police.
A police officer said the complainant had submitted WhatsApp conversations, mobile phone numbers, screenshots of the video call, gift card details and transaction records as evidence. He also provided a UPI ID, sumanaghosh221122@oksbi, suspected to be linked to the transactions.
A case has been registered at the East Cyber Crime police station under the Information Technology Act and Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Box
How to stay away from dating app scamsBe cautious with strangers:
 Avoid intimate video calls with people you have just met on dating apps or social media platforms.
Protect your identity:
 Avoid sharing intimate photographs or videos with strangers. Be mindful that video calls can be recorded without your knowledge or consent.
Don’t give in to threats:
 Do not panic or pay money in response to blackmail threats, even if fraudsters threaten to contact your family, friends or colleagues.
Never share financial details:
 Do not purchase or share gift card codes, OTPs, UPI PINs, banking credentials or other financial information at the request of strangers.
Block and report suspicious accounts:
 Report suspicious profiles on dating apps and messaging platforms.
Report financial fraud immediately:
 If you have transferred money, contact your bank immediately and report the incident by calling the cybercrime helpline 1930. You can also file a complaint through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in).

briefs.headline: From bamboo groves to thematic forests, 10 tree parks proposed for Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The plan involves removing eucalyptus and acacia plantations from identified areas and replacing them with indigenous tree species.
briefs.bodyText:
The State Forest Department has proposed developing 10 “tree parks” across 3,271 acres of forest land and research areas in Bengaluru at an indicative cost of ₹222 crore. The proposal is expected to be placed before the State Cabinet on November 30 for in-principle approval.
The proposal comes after several months of the government inspecting and identifying land for the parks, following D.K. Shivakumar assuming office as Chief Minister. The government officials had earlier indicated that the idea was to develop spaces along the lines of Cubbon Park and Lalbagh Botanical Garden.
‘Expand green cover’
Minister for Forest Ramalinga Reddy told The Hindu that Bengaluru, with a population of over one crore, did not have enough parks and green spaces to meet the needs of its residents. The aim was to expand the city’s green cover, he said, adding that the Forest Department hoped to complete work on all 10 parks within a year with support from the government and CSR funds. Several organisations had already expressed interest in supporting the projects, the Minister added.
The plan involves removing eucalyptus and acacia plantations from identified areas and replacing them with indigenous tree species. The proposal accessed by The Hindu explained that this is necessary to increase Bengaluru’s green cover and restore its identity as the Garden City. It also lists biodiversity conservation, groundwater recharge through rainwater infiltration and reducing the urban heat island effect among its objectives.
Of the 3,271 acres identified across the nine locations, 1,303 acres will be developed for public access, while the remaining 1,968 acres will be taken up for ecological restoration and conservation. The removal of alien species, however, will be undertaken only after approval of the respective work plans.
Features
The proposed parks will have walking, trekking and cycling trails, thematic tree plantations, medicinal plant gardens and spaces for environmental education. The larger portions of the identified forest areas will be retained for restoration, with activities such as planting indigenous species, grassland development and rainwater harvesting, the proposal stated.
The locations include two forest blocks at Turahalli, the Kalkere Forest Ecology Centre inside Bannerghatta National Park, Doresanipalya Forest Research and Extension Centre, Marasandra, Mandur, Panathur and two blocks at Jarakabande.
Location-wise plans
The proposed parks will have distinct features, including six thematic forests and restored ponds at Turahalli, a bamboo species collection at Mandur and an expanded biodiversity park at Panathur. At Jarakabande, A Block will have a tree cultivation and research centre for farmers and tree growers, while B Block will see the existing urban forest upgraded. The proposal also includes facilities like groundwater recharge pits and herbal garden at Kalkere centre, inside Bannerghatta National Park, and replacing exotic trees with indigenous species at several sites.
The Jarakabande Tree Cultivation Centre in A Block has the highest allocation of over ₹35 crore, followed by the Kalkere Forest Ecology Centre at ₹21.91 crore. The two Turahalli projects have been estimated to cost over ₹16 crore each.
After in-principle approval, the department will prepare Detailed Project Reports for each location and seek administrative approval with the concurrence of the Finance Department. The works are proposed to be funded in phases from 2026-27 through State Budget allocations and CSR funds. Revenue from entry tickets would be retained for the maintenance of each park, the proposal said.
The proposal also lists the 154-acre Vishwaguru Basavanna Biodiversity Park at Madappanahalli in North Bengaluru. However, the park had already received the Cabinet approval in January, with an initial funding of ₹50 crore during Eshwar Khandre’s tenure as the Forest Minister.

stories.headline: Megaspeed, Singaporean company at heart of Nvidia scandal, added to U.S. export control list
stories.deck: Jensen Huang, 63, stepped down from Nvidia after reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation, a former executive at Megaspeed
stories.bodyText:
The United States on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed International to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was accused of having an affair with a Megaspeed executive alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The company, along with four affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, was added to the U.S. Commerce Department's Entity List for "acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States," the department said in a filing on the Federal Register.
Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down after reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation, a former executive at Megaspeed, which bought billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips.
He was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO on Monday morning, after U.S. President Donald Trump repeatedly insisted he should return to lead a company at the center of the AI revolution.
Monday's designation bars Megaspeed from buying AI chips and other advanced technology without a U.S. government license.
The company has been accused of possibly funneling high-end chips and computing power to China, in contravention of strict U.S. export controls.
U.S. intelligence services have reportedly concluded Alice Huang passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.
Among the seven firms added to the entity list on Monday were Singapore-based Swiftdata, which is Megaspeed's holding company, and Megaspeed affiliate Speedmatrix, based in Malaysia.
Monday's move comes after the Trump administration announced tougher export controls on AI chips last week, closing a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's most advanced chips remotely.

stories.headline: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
stories.deck: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?
stories.bodyText:
The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission. On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms.
The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support.
Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models.
On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models.
Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API).

stories.headline: Property seller takes Rs 6.75 lakh cash payment, faces 100% penalty; ITAT cancels it
stories.deck: The man faced action from the Income Tax Department after he sold his residential property for Rs 32 lakh to a senior citizen. The issue arose when the property seller accepted Rs 6.75 lakh of the sale consideration in cash, with the balance being paid into his bank account. The payment arrangement was also recorded in the registered sale deed.
stories.bodyText:
Can you accept cash above a certain limit for a property sale? The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai, has directed the Income Tax Department to delete a Rs 6.75 lakh penalty imposed on a property seller who accepted an advance in cash towards the sale of his residential property.
The man faced action from the Income Tax Department after he sold his residential property for Rs 32 lakh to a senior citizen.
The tribunal held that the circumstances surrounding the transaction established reasonable cause under Section 273B of the Income-tax Act, 1961, providing relief from the penalty imposed under Section 271D.
What the case is about
The issue arose when the property seller accepted Rs 6.75 lakh of the sale consideration in cash, with the balance being paid into his bank account. The payment arrangement was also recorded in the registered sale deed.
However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) initiated proceedings after receiving information from the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) in Virugambakkam and examining the registered sale deed. The AO concluded that accepting the cash payment violated Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act and issued a notice.
The home seller said he needed to sell his house urgently and had approached a broker to find a buyer. 
The broker subsequently located a senior citizen who agreed to visit Chennai to inspect the property.
When the prospective buyer arrived, he was carrying Rs 6.75 lakh in cash. After viewing the house, he liked the property and made an offer to purchase it immediately. To finalise the deal, he proposed paying Rs 6.75 lakh as an advance in cash.
The buyer told the home seller that he did not want to take the money all the way back, nor did he wish to postpone the transaction until he could arrange payment through banking channels.
The home seller said he weighed his urgent need to sell the property against the buyer's circumstances. He also believed that refusing the cash would leave the senior citizen with the risk of carrying Rs 6.75 lakh back. He therefore accepted the amount in good faith.
He maintained that he had disclosed the cash payment in the sale deed and reported the entire property transaction in his income tax return (ITR), believing that these disclosures would meet the requirements of the Income Tax Act.
Of the total sale price of Rs 32 lakh, Rs 6.75 lakh was received in cash as an advance, while the remaining consideration was paid into his bank account. The full sale amount was documented in the sale deed.
The proceedings culminated in a penalty of Rs 6.75 lakh being imposed on the home seller for accepting cash in connection with the property sale.
He challenged the penalty and secured a favourable ruling from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai.
Why did ITAT Chennai rule in favour of the property seller?
One of the key considerations was that the man had not attempted to hide the cash component of the property sale. He had disclosed the payment in the registered sale deed, reported the transaction in his income tax return (ITR), deposited the money in his bank account and paid capital gains tax after disclosing the transaction.
The tribunal examined whether the man qualified for relief under Section 273B of the Income Tax Act, which provides protection from penalties when a taxpayer can demonstrate reasonable cause for failing to comply with the law.
The ITAT considered the seller’s explanation alongside the circumstances surrounding the transaction. It noted that the CIT(A) had not disputed the genuineness of the sale, the deposit of the advance into the seller’s bank account, the receipt of the balance consideration through banking channels or the recording of the full consideration in the registered sale deed.
The tribunal cautioned that these circumstances did not independently establish reasonable cause. However, it considered them material when assessing the seller’s explanation collectively. It observed: “Although these circumstances do not, individually, establish reasonable cause, they are material factors supporting the assessee's explanation regarding the bona fide circumstances in which the cash advance was accepted.”
The bench found that the CIT(A) had not adequately assessed the combined effect of these circumstances while deciding whether the seller qualified for relief under Section 273B. It held: “Consequently, the conclusion reached by the ld.CIT(A) that the assessee had failed to establish reasonable cause cannot be sustained on the facts and circumstances of the present case.”
The tribunal also considered earlier decisions of the Chennai and Visakhapatnam benches involving cash received towards property sales. Its discussion included the Supreme Court’s decision in 
Hindustan Steel Ltd. v. State of Orissa
, which formed part of the legal background concerning the imposition of penalties. The decisive finding in this case, however, was that the seller had established reasonable cause under Section 273B when the circumstances were considered together.
The ITAT concluded: “The contravention of section 269SS of the Act, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, is therefore covered by the statutory protection provided u/s.273B of the Act.”
Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that ITAT held that Section 269SS did not apply to this case. It also clarified that a breach of Section 269SS does not, by itself, automatically establish a violation of Section 271D.
Surana said the assessee’s actions lent credibility to his explanation that he had accepted the cash because he genuinely believed the senior citizen buyer’s account of his circumstances. They also supported his contention that he had no intention of suppressing or concealing the transaction.
Surana said the ruling highlights how Section 273B can offer protection from penalties when a taxpayer provides a genuine and reasonable explanation for accepting cash in a property transaction and transparently records the payment in the ITR, sale deed and other relevant documents.

briefs.headline: Google denies rumours of large-scale layoffs in India
briefs.deck: An official Google handle on X noted that “approximately 30 roles were eliminated”
briefs.bodyText:
Google has shot down social media rumours about secret, large-scale employee layoffs taking place in India.
An official Google handle on X noted that only around 30 roles were affected and that the rumours of larger layoffs were untrue.
“These rumours are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organisational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritisation of work,” posted the company in response to a user on X on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
The source of this updated information was the Google Cloud India official handle on the X (formerly Twitter) social media platform. The handle had been verified as an official organisation.
The original X user had claimed there were “huge” layoffs at Google India and asked what was happening, while other social media users earlier shared unverified claims about Google employees panicking or being given layoff notices.
Indian tech and IT employees are facing yet another period of instability; this was underscored by Microsoft last month offering voluntary exit packages to around 60,000 staff members, including eligible Indian teams.
The number represented about a quarter of the company’s workforce.
Google has also expanded its voluntary buyout initiative to more countries.

briefs.headline: Stock market holiday today: Are BSE, NSE closed on November 24 for Guru Nanak Jayanti
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The 
BSE
 and 
NSE
 will remain closed on Tuesday, November 24, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev or 
Guru Nanak Jayanti
. Commodity trading on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), however, will resume during the evening session.
This is the second-last stock market holiday of 2026, with the final one scheduled for December 25 on account of Christmas.
Why are NSE and BSE closed today?
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) have declared November 24 a trading holiday for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev, also known as Guru Nanak Jayanti.
Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives, securities lending and borrowing (SLB), capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market segments.
The MCX will follow a partial trading schedule, with its morning session closed from 9 am to 5 pm. Trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11.30 pm.
The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) will remain closed for the entire day.
The holiday comes after a sharp sell-off in domestic equities on Monday, with both benchmark indices declining nearly 1.8% amid heavy selling in banking and metal stocks, weakness in global markets and profit booking following the recent rally.
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65, down 450.95 points or 1.75%, while the BSE Sensex settled at 82,435.99, declining 1,483.72 points or 1.77%.
Selling pressure was broad-based, with banking and commodity stocks bearing the brunt of the decline. The Nifty Bank index fell more than 3% to 62,585 after recently touching an all-time high, while the Nifty Metal index recorded the steepest sectoral decline, shedding 3.70%.
The Nifty IT index was the only major sectoral index to close in positive territory, gaining 1.8%.
When will stock market trading resume?
Trading on the NSE and BSE will resume on Wednesday, November 25, with regular market hours. The MCX will also operate its regular morning and evening sessions on Wednesday, while the NCDEX will resume trading after the holiday.
The next and final scheduled stock market holiday of the year will be December 25 for Christmas, apart from regular weekend closures.
Global markets rebound after Wall Street rally
Asian shares surged on Tuesday following a strong rally on Wall Street, as technology and AI-related stocks rebounded sharply after recent losses.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6%, recovering from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks.
Japan's Nikkei rose 4.5% as traders returned after a local holiday, while South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5% and Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1%.
Nvidia shares rallied 31.5% on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in market value. The rally also lifted other AI-related stocks, with the Nasdaq 100 jumping more than 6%.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite surged 4.7% and 6.5%, respectively, while S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2% early on Tuesday.
Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling 3.5% lower at $89.37 on Monday. Gold also recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot prices rising 0.7% to $3,657.97 an ounce as investors bought the dip.

briefs.headline: Brookfield to buy PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Global investment firm Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity for $1.7 billion.
The transaction, which is subject to regulatory and govt approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Brookfield will fund the acquisition through its Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation.
PGP Glass manufactures premium glass packaging for cosmetics, perfumes, pharmaceuticals and specialty food and beverages. The company operates three manufacturing facilities across India and Sri Lanka and supplies packaging to global brands in more than 70 countries.
The company has 13 furnaces and a production capacity of more than 1,800 tonnes per day. Overseas markets account for more than 70% of its sales. Brookfield plans to expand PGP Glass's presence in international markets, deepen relationships with existing customers and invest in additional manufacturing capacity. It also intends to introduce artificial intelligence across the company's operations, including production planning, manufacturing efficiency and quality control.
Aditya Joshi, managing partner and head of private equity for Brookfield in Asia Pacific and the Middle East, said, "As demand for high-quality packaging continues to increase worldwide, Brookfield brings the scale and operating expertise to accelerate PGP's growth through an AI-led transformation program."
The investment comes as glass packaging manufacturers in Europe and North America face rising costs and rationalise capacity. Brookfield sees an opportunity for manufacturers such as PGP, which have lower production costs, to gain market share in premium packaging.
Blackstone said its investment in PGP had helped the company expand manufacturing capacity, improve operations and strengthen its sustainability initiatives.
Amit Dalmia, senior managing director and head of the Blackstone Operating Team in Asia, said the company's management had delivered strong operating performance and outpaced its peers during Blackstone's ownership. PGP Glass CEO Vijay Shah said Brookfield's international presence and operational experience would support the company's next phase of growth. He also credited Blackstone's partnership with helping PGP expand capacity and strengthen its operations.
